summary: Added programs.sapience.sessionClassifier, exporting the vendor's NO_CLASSIFY=1 switch, wired into both module trees (modules/home/services/sapience.nix at default false, packages/sapience-flake at default true/vendor-matching), with a classifier-aware progress ticker in both. Applied via home-manager switch and recorded the measured per-pass cost shape in docs/sapience.md as settled fact.

artifacts.summary: Implementation summary covering all 4 phases, decisions, deviations, and verification evidence.

completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented the NO_CLASSIFY=1 lever as a new programs.sapience.sessionClassifier module option in both sapience trees (dotfiles module default false, standalone flake default true), with a classifier-aware ticker, applied the change live via home-manager switch, and recorded the measured per-pass cost shape (classifier dominates roughly the first 20 of 29 minutes per pass; the classify-eligible backlog holds flat at 136 and does not drain) in docs/sapience.md as settled fact.

sapience_notes.subject: Sapience classifier-cost reduction lever choice
sapience_notes.value: NO_CLASSIFY=1 via a new module option, not verdict caching across runs -- verdict caching would require patching the vendor's self-updating ~/.sapience/extract_local.py payload, which sapience update's daily auto_update() silently overwrites within a day.

sapience_notes.subject: Sapience extraction classifier wall-clock cost
sapience_notes.value: A real extraction pass on the anthropic backend spent roughly the first 20 of 29 total wall-clock minutes in the work/personal classifier phase (71 sources extracted, 1208 knowledge objects staged, only 3.5s of CPU total, entirely network-bound). A fresh sapience coverage reading on 2026-11-18 held flat at 136 ('would ingest now') both before and after applying a classifier-disabling fix, confirming the classify-eligible backlog does not self-drain.

sapience_notes.subject: Nix-generated shell script comment vs grep-based built-artifact verification
sapience_notes.value: A prose comment inside a Nix-generated shell script that contains the exact literal string a later grep-based built-artifact check searches for (e.g. 'NO_CLASSIFY=1') is counted by that grep exactly like a real export statement, silently inflating an 'exactly N occurrences' check. Avoid reusing the literal searched string in nearby prose.

sapience_notes.subject: GitHub-flavored-markdown anchor generation for a slash in a heading
sapience_notes.value: GFM anchor generation strips a slash entirely rather than converting it to a hyphen. A heading like '### The work/personal classifier is off' renders as anchor '#the-workpersonal-classifier-is-off', not '#the-work-personal-classifier-is-off'.

sapience_notes.subject: dotfiles repo shell-test-battery baseline staleness
sapience_notes.value: test-lint-state-writer-boundary.sh, failing in a measured baseline sweep of this repo's shell test battery recorded on 2026-11-18, passed cleanly (27 passed, 0 failed) when re-run directly later the same day -- an unrelated fix landed between the two measurements, illustrating how quickly a recorded test-suite baseline here can go stale.

sapience_notes.subject: Sapience parallel module-tree vendor-toggle convention
sapience_notes.value: This repository mirrors a vendor env-var toggle across its two hand-maintained parallel Sapience module trees (modules/home/services/sapience.nix, the live machine config, and packages/sapience-flake, the published standalone flake) using the identical option name in both but DIFFERENT defaults -- the published flake matches the vendor default, the dotfiles module flips it with a machine-specific measured rationale in the option description. memoryFiles/NO_MEMFILES established this; sessionClassifier/NO_CLASSIFY now follows it.
